layers.process: Vicente Pérez Rosales National Park (Osorno and Llanquihue provinces; Chile's oldest national park, created 1926): CONAF directs visitors to its Pases Parques ticket site for entry tickets, opening hours and visit conditions, and says official information is available only from CONAF and Pases Parques. Prices were not read.
Chiloé National Park (communes of Ancud, Dalcahue, Castro and Chonchi): entry tickets, hours and conditions through CONAF's Pases Parques site. Prices were not read.

Alerce Andino National Park (Puerto Montt and Cochamó): CONAF lists these trails as closed until further notice: Laguna Sargazo, Laguna Fría, Catedral de Alerce, Rodal de Alerce, Laguna Triángulo and Laguna Chaiquenes. Entry tickets are through Pases Parques.

Puyehue National Park (Valdivia and Osorno provinces; communes Puyehue and Puerto Octay are in Los Lagos, Río Bueno and Lago Ranco in Los Ríos): open Monday to Sunday 9:00 to 17:30, no booking system. Entry to the trails is free, except the concessioned trails El Indio, Repucura and La Princesa. Prices for those were not read.

Puyehue National Park: for long-distance treks you must ask the park administrator for authorisation by email (address on CONAF's park page). Anyone heading into the mountains must tell the rangers before leaving and receive an ascent form recording personal and group details. Boats in the park are limited to rowing boats for fishing and recreation.

laws.rule: Puyehue National Park: drones are not allowed inside the park, except for professional research or filming with CONAF's prior authorisation (CONAF's published park rules).

Puyehue National Park: any heat source is banned (barbecues, campfires, gas stoves, cigarettes) and CONAF cites Law 20.653, article 22. Pets and exotic animals can't enter. Visitors must stay on the trails and follow the rangers' directions.
Puyehue National Park: smoking, drinking alcohol and using drugs or other hallucinogenic products are banned in the park (CONAF's published park rules).

Parque Nacional Corcovado: The operator says the park has no visitor assistance or public-use infrastructure. This is not a promise of routine tourist access or an assertion that all entry is legally banned. The named unit prohibits fires and other heat sources, pets or exotic animals, leaving enabled trails and removing natural resources. Follow ranger instructions; no region-wide extension is made.

items.text: Parque Nacional Corcovado: CONAF's own unit page prohibits consuming alcoholic drinks. This is the named protected-area condition, not an alcohol ban throughout the region.

Parque Nacional Corcovado: smoking is prohibited in CONAF's published unit conditions. The same page prohibits consuming drugs or hallucinogenic products; no wider possession or prescribing rule is inferred.
